title: Graph Data Modeling 101 | Martin O'Hanlon | Connected Data London 2025
description:
Graph databases give the same importance to relationships as they do to data. Knowledge graphs allow you to uncover insights in your data and efficiently explore the relationships in your data.

In this hands-on workshop you will learn how graph databases can help you find and understand relationships in your data

You will:
Learn about graph theory, the elements of a graph database, and when a graph database is a good choice for your use case.
Explore a graph database, learn the basics of the query language Cypher, and use Cypher to read and write data.
Import your data into a graph database.



Key Topics
Graph databases and the underlying principles.
How to read and write data using Cypher.
Patterns matching and how to use it to find data in a graph.
How to aggregate data and asking questions of your data.
How to create a data graph model for your data.
How to import data to create:
A data model.
Nodes, relationships, and properties.
Indexes and constraints.


Target Audience
Data Scientists
Data Analysts
Software developers
Managers of the above


Goals
Get hands-on experience using Neo4j graph database to understand relationships, query and create data.


Session outline:
Introduction to graph database fundamentals
Graph database use cases and considerations
Reading and writing data from a graph
Pattern matching
Graph data modelling
Importing data


Format
This class is very hands-on.
You will be using Neo4j and the GraphAcademy platform to explore a graph database.
The masterclass will start with an overview of graph and graph database fundamentals and concepts.
You will write queries to find, filter, aggregate and analyse data.
You will import data into an empty database, creating your own data model, and explore how you can import your own data into a graph.


Level
Beginner



Prerequisite Knowledge
There are no pre-requisites for attendees, however the workshop is best suited to those who have some experience of working with databases.

Attendees should bring their own laptop, which they will need to access the online workshop material, and, supplied, database. There is no software to pre-install, learners will only need access to a web browser.
